title: Euler characteristic of finite images of a family of smooth proper curves
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $X$ be a proper $k$-scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $I$ be a finite set. For each $i\in I$, let $C_i$ be a smooth proper connected curve over $k$ [def-sc-curves] and let $h_i:C_i\to X$ be a finite $k$-morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Put $C=\coprod_{i\in I}C_i$, let $h:C\to X$ restrict to $h_i$ on $C_i$, and put $G_i=h_{i,*}\mathcal O_{C_i}$ and $B=h_*\mathcal O_C$, where direct image means sections $G_i(U)=\mathcal O_{C_i}(h_i^{-1}U)$ in the category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then $G_i$ and $B$ are coherent [pqf-def-coherent], and restriction to the summands induces an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules
$$B\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\prod_{i\in I}G_i=\bigoplus_{i\in I}G_i.$$
For every $q\ge0$, the edge map $e_{h_i,\mathcal O_{C_i}}$ of [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap](c), induced by the $h_i$-map $\mathrm{id}_{G_i}$, is a $k$-linear isomorphism
$$H^q(X,G_i)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^q(C_i,\mathcal O_{C_i})$$
[def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. The structure map $k\to H^0(C_i,\mathcal O_{C_i})$ is an isomorphism, and $H^q(C_i,\mathcal O_{C_i})=0$ for $q>1$. Writing $g_i=\dim_kH^1(C_i,\mathcal O_{C_i})$ [def-sc-genus], the Euler characteristics [def-pc-euler-characteristic] satisfy
$$\chi(X,G_i)=\chi(C_i,\mathcal O_{C_i})=1-g_i,\qquad\chi(X,B)=|I|-\sum_{i\in I}g_i.$$
This includes the empty family, for which $B=0$ and $\chi(X,B)=0$. No component-embedding, birationality, reducedness or dimension hypothesis on $X$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 089W (lemma-relative-affine-cohomology), affine edge isomorphisms; varieties.tex Tag 08AA (lemma-euler-characteristic-additive), finite-sum additivity; curves.tex Tag 0BY7 (definition-genus).

proof.text: The structure module $\mathcal O_Y$ is invertible: its identity trivialization is a rank-one trivialization [def-sc-invertible-module]. Apply [lem-trf-proper-field-invertible-coherent] with $Y=X$ and with $Y=C_i$. Thus $X,C_i$ are Noetherian and their structure modules are coherent. Since $h_i$ is finite and $X$ is locally Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-coherent] makes $G_i=h_{i,*}\mathcal O_{C_i}$ coherent. In particular $\mathcal O_{C_i}$ is quasi-coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth].

For each open $U\subseteq X$, the opens $h_i^{-1}U$ form a disjoint open cover of $h^{-1}U$. The sheaf axiom gives $\mathcal O_C(h^{-1}U)\cong\prod_i\mathcal O_{C_i}(h_i^{-1}U)$ by restriction; its inverse glues the given sections, whose compatibility on empty intersections is automatic. Restriction commutes with restriction to smaller $U$, and the scalar action in each coordinate is through $h_i^\sharp$. These are therefore the asserted $\mathcal O_X$-linear sheaf isomorphism. For finite $I$, a tuple is the sum of its coordinate inclusions, so this product is also the direct sum. Binary sum closure in [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth](1), iterated over the finite set, gives coherence of $B$; the empty sum is the zero coherent module directly from the definition.

source.place: Tag 01Y0 (lemma-coherent-abelian-Noetherian); product identification is the sheaf axiom on the disjoint union.

proof.text: Finite morphisms are affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-cohomology-edge] to $h_i$ and the quasi-coherent module $\mathcal O_{C_i}$. Its statement identifies exactly the identity-$h_i$-map edge map in the question and makes it an isomorphism linear over $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Restrict scalars along $k\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$: because $h_i$ is a $k$-morphism, the composite into $\Gamma(C_i,\mathcal O_{C_i})$ is its structure map. Thus these are precisely the stated $k$-linear isomorphisms in every degree.

source.place: Tag 089W (lemma-relative-affine-cohomology), via Tag 01XC and Cohomology Tag 01F4; linearity is scalar restriction.

proof.text: For each $i$, [lem-sc-global-functions] explicitly includes proper smooth connected curves over an algebraically closed field, so its structure map $k\to H^0(C_i,\mathcal O_{C_i})$ is an isomorphism. By [def-sc-curves], $\dim C_i=1$. The Noetherianity from Step 1 permits [lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-above-dimension] with $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_{C_i}$ and any $q>1$, giving the required vanishing.

source.place: Tag 02UZ (proposition-vanishing-Noetherian); global functions as in varieties.tex, lemma-proper-geometrically-reduced-global-sections.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-euler-characteristic-well-defined] to $G_i$ on $X$ and to $\mathcal O_{C_i}$ on $C_i$, both coherent and proper as established above. The Euler sums are finite. The $k$-linear isomorphisms of Step 3 equate every dimension and therefore equate the sums. On $C_i$, Step 4 makes the degree-zero dimension $1$ and all degrees above one zero. The remaining dimension is $g_i$ by [def-sc-genus]. Substitution into [def-pc-euler-characteristic] yields $\chi(X,G_i)=\chi(C_i,\mathcal O_{C_i})=1-g_i$.

source.place: Tag 0BY7 (definition-genus) and the following arithmetic-genus formula; finiteness as in varieties.tex, definition-euler-characteristic.

proof.text: For coherent modules $F,G$ the maps $f\mapsto(f,0)$ and $(f,g)\mapsto g$ give the split short exact sequence $0\to F\to F\oplus G\to G\to0$. Apply the short-exact-sequence clause of [lem-pc-euler-additive] on the proper scheme $X$ and induct on the finite set $I$, using the coherent partial sums from Step 2. This gives $\chi(X,B)=\sum_i\chi(X,G_i)=\sum_i(1-g_i)=|I|-\sum_i g_i$. If $I$ is empty, the sheaf axiom on the empty cover makes every section module of $B$ zero; a zero injective resolution computes zero cohomology, so its Euler sum is zero. This supplies the induction base and the stated empty-family case.

source.place: Tag 08AA (lemma-euler-characteristic-additive), applied to the displayed split sequences.
